$comment: The area registry (docs/test-explorer-spec.md §5, amended by §2a/§2c/§2d). Rows are feature areas in product language, matching the outer `describe` convention in testing-strategy.md §9.1 - undotted, not an entity ('Triage', not 'item.setStatus'). A source file can legitimately match more than one area's sourcePatterns (e.g. apps/api/src/domain/items.ts backs Capture, Triage and Offline as different functions in one file) - that is expected, not an overlap error. `pnpm --filter @cockpit/test-explorer check-concepts` instead fails when a test declares an area missing from this file. A file matching zero areas falls into 'infrastructure' automatically. Concepts with an empty sourcePatterns list are declared ahead of the code that will eventually own them and stay at zero everywhere until then. Glob syntax: '*' within a path segment, '**' across segments. The nine top-level areas are testing-strategy.md §9.1's own example list verbatim. An entry can carry an optional "parent": "<key>" naming another entry's key, turning the flat list into a tree - a real feature area that's grown too big for one row gets children this way rather than being renamed in every test that already uses it. Dashboards > Drag-drop / Resizing below are a placeholder demonstrating the shape (docs/test-explorer-spec.md §2d point 1) - no test names either describe yet, so both stay at zero everywhere until real tests do, same as any other empty-sourcePatterns entry, and either can be renamed or removed freely once real sub-areas are known. Every other entry's children should still match real describe names, not a guess made ahead of the code.
